prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1 (ATMEGA328P-PU, DIP-28) sits on the synthetic CircuitOS:DIP-28 footprint at (20.32,22.86). That footprint has exactly the same pad pattern as KiCad 10 stock Package_DIP:DIP-28_W7.62mm after a Y flip, and is equal to it under no rotation and no X mirror: the stock puts pad 1 at the notched end with the numbers running down the left column, this one runs the other way. A DIP-28 is insertable only with its single notch at the pad-1/pad-28 end, and the die pin 1 sits to the left of that notch, so the die pin 1 lands in the hole the file labels 28 and the die pin 28 in the hole the file labels 1 (die pin = 29 - board pad). The board therefore puts VCC_5V on the die pin 22 (GND/AGND) and GND on the die pin 7 (VCC), while the die's own grounds (pins 8 and 22) land in a netless hole and on VCC_5V. The chip is reverse-powered: 5 V into AGND, 0 V into VCC, and it is dead on arrival. No rotation of the part fixes it, because the notch end is fixed by the package.
expected: A DIP-28 footprint whose pin-1 hole, notch and silkscreen agree with the datasheet, so the ATmega's pin 7 is VCC, pins 8 and 22 are GND, pin 20 is AVCC, and the pin-1 dot sits at the notch.
evidence: evidence_board_02/dip_check.py (product == stock mirrored in Y: True; product == stock: False; mirrored in X: False; rotated 180: False); evidence_board_02/u1_map_output.txt; evidence_board_02/u1_pin_map.json

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The net that drives the transistor base is broken in mid-air. The F.Cu track coming from R2 ends at (35.1121,31.8321); the track running down to Q1's base pad ends at (34.6879,31.4079). The two ends are 0.5999 mm apart, so there is no copper between the 1 kOhm base resistor and the base of the 2N2222A. My own copper graph resolves RELAY_CTRL into two components (Q1.2 with the tracks below it, R2.2 with the tracks above it), and KiCad's DRC reports the same pair as an unconnected item at severity error. The break survives a zone refill, so it is a routing break, not a pour artefact, and the same gap is already in the product's own board_ir.json (RELAY_CTRL track list ends (34.6879,14.3121) and starts (35.1121,13.8879) in the IR's mirrored y), so the break is upstream of the .kicad_pcb writer.
expected: One continuous copper path from the base resistor to Q1's base pin.
evidence: evidence_board_02/facts_output.txt section 4 (the two segments and the 0.5999 mm gap); evidence_board_02/connectivity_analysis.json (net_components.RELAY_CTRL = 2 components); evidence_board_02/drc_independent.json (unconnected item: Track[RELAY_CTRL] F.Cu len 3.8012 @(32.0,28.72) <-> Track[RELAY_CTRL] F.Cu len 3.8012 @(35.112132,31.832132))

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board's only zone is named plane GND, on B.Cu, for net GND, and it declares (fill yes ...), but the file contains no filled_polygon block at all: the zone was delivered with no copper in it. Every ground point therefore hangs on its own stub and GND is not one node. My copper graph resolves GND into five separate islands: (C1.2 + via 12.60,35.52), (Q1.1 + via 28.00,24.12), (U1.8 + via 16.60,21.52), (U1.22 + via 24.20,24.12), (U2.4 + via 10.20,21.72). The ATmega's two ground pins are not tied together, the transistor's emitter is not tied to the sensor's ground, and the sensor's ground is not tied to anything else. KiCad's DRC reports 5 via_dangling violations and 4 unconnected GND items; refilling a copy of this file removes every one of them, which pins the cause on the undelivered fill rather than on the routing.
expected: A filled ground pour, or tracks, that tie all five ground points into a single node.
evidence: evidence_board_02/connectivity_analysis.json (net_components.GND = 5 components); evidence_board_02/drc_independent.json; evidence_board_02/drc_refilled.json (after refill: 1 unconnected item, the RELAY_CTRL break, and no via_dangling); evidence_board_02/render_bottom.png (kicad-cli 3D render of the bottom side: pads and vias only, no ground copper anywhere)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: K1 sits on a synthetic CircuitOS:RELAY-SRD footprint: two rows of holes 15.0 mm apart (x = -7.5 and +7.5) with 5.0 mm spacing inside each row, drill 1.1 mm. The Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C in its datasheet drawing has three pins on one side and two on the other, 2.54 mm pitch, the two rows 7.62 mm apart, holes about 1.0 mm. A real relay's pins do not fall into this board's holes: the rows are twice as far apart as the part's and the pitch is double, so the part cannot be fitted to this footprint at all.
expected: A footprint whose hole pattern is the part's hole pattern.
evidence: evidence_board_02/footprint_geometry.json (CircuitOS:RELAY-SRD pads at x = -7.5/+7.5, y = -5/0/+5); Songle mini-relay-05VDC-SL-C datasheet mechanical drawing (2.54 mm pin pitch, 7.62 mm between the two rows, body about 19.0 x 15.5 x 15.3 mm)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board drives the relay coil between K1 pad 1 (VCC_5V) and K1 pad 2 (RELAY_COIL_NEG), and leaves K1 pads 3, 4 and 5 on no net. The Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C datasheet's bottom view puts the coil on pins 2 and 5, one on each side, with 1 = COM, 3 = NC and 4 = NO. So the board puts a supply rail on the COM contact, the second coil terminal (pin 5) is left floating, and the SPDT contacts reach nothing at all: the relay can neither be energised nor switch anything.
expected: The coil across the two coil pins, and COM, NO and NC each carried on a net that leaves the board.
evidence: evidence_board_02/connectivity_analysis.json (K1 pads 3, 4 and 5 netless); board_02.kicad_pcb pad net assignments for K1; Songle mini-relay-05VDC-SL-C datasheet bottom-view pinout (1 COM, 2 Coil, 3 NC, 4 NO, 5 Coil)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: Q1 sits on CircuitOS:TO-92 whose three leads are at x = -2.54, 0, +2.54 mm, i.e. 2.54 mm lead pitch, and the Board IR declares a 7.98 x 2.9 mm courtyard for it. The TO-92 outline in the 2N2222A datasheet gives adjacent lead pitch e = 1.270 mm typ (outer span 2.44-2.64 mm) and a body 3.3-3.7 mm tall and 4.3-4.7 mm wide, so the leads of a standard-pitch 2N2222A do not line up with these holes, and the body is taller than the courtyard drawn around it. Bound: some vendors ship a 2.54 mm-pitch 2N2222A variant and the Board IR names only 2N2222A, so whether the transistor fits depends on which part is actually bought - but the footprint matches neither the standard part nor KiCad's own stock TO-92 (1.27 mm).
expected: A TO-92 footprint at the part's 1.27 mm lead pitch with a courtyard that contains the 4.3-4.7 mm by 3.3-3.7 mm body.
evidence: evidence_board_02/footprint_geometry.json (CircuitOS:TO-92 pads at -2.54/0/+2.54); board_ir.json courtyard for Q1 (7.98 x 2.9); 2N2222A TO-92 datasheet outline (TRR/Diotec: e = 1.270 TYP, A = 3.300-3.700, D = 4.300-4.700)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request asked for an LED on the board. The board has eight footprints - U1 ATMEGA328P-PU, U2 DHT22, K1 SRD-05VDC-SL-C, Q1 2N2222A, D1 1N4007, R1 CFR-25JB-52-10K, R2 CFR-25JB-52-1K, C1 K104K15X7RF53H5 - and no LED among them. The string LED occurs nowhere in board_02.kicad_pcb (the only match is the substring inside filled_areas_thickness) and nowhere in board_ir.json. There is no LED net, no LED footprint and no LED current-limiting resistor: R1 is the DHT22 data pull-up and R2 the base resistor, so nothing in the design lights anything. The product returned a board for a request it silently did not build.
expected: An LED with its series current-limiting resistor driven from a GPIO.
evidence: evidence_board_02/facts_output.txt section 8 (LED: 0 occurrences in board_02.kicad_pcb, 0 in board_ir.json); the eight-footprint list in board_02.kicad_pcb

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.

The 2 metre sensor cable and its connector are simply absent from the design.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1's crystal pins (board pads 9 and 10 = PB6/XTAL1 and PB7/XTAL2) and AREF (pad 21) are on no net, and the board carries no crystal, no 16 MHz source, no ICSP programming header, no USB or serial interface, no regulator, no reset circuit and no headers. The request asked for an Arduino Uno; what is on the board is a bare ATmega328P-PU with no clock and no way to program it. An ATmega328P ships with CKDIV8 programmed, so with no crystal the part runs its internal RC at 1 MHz, not the 16 MHz any Uno-targeted firmware assumes.
expected: The Uno's own circuitry, or at minimum a crystal across XTAL1/XTAL2 and a programming header.
evidence: evidence_board_02/connectivity_analysis.json (U1 pads 9, 10 and 21 netless); evidence_board_02/facts_output.txt section 8 (no XTAL, crystal, ICSP or Uno string in board_02.kicad_pcb); Microchip ATmega328P datasheet (CKDIV8 = 1 MHz default)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The Board IR gives U2 a courtyard of 8.2 x 15.6 mm, but the AM2302/DHT22 body is 25.1 x 15.1 x 7.7 mm, so the sensor overhangs its own courtyard by 16.9 mm along its long axis. U2's pin row is at x = 10.12 mm, only 6.4 mm from the ATmega's pin column, and the ATmega's courtyard starts at x = 14.8 mm, so the sensor's body reaches the microcontroller. There is also no marking of which way round the sensor goes, so the orientation is undefined as well.
expected: A courtyard that contains the sensor's body, and a marked orientation.
evidence: evidence_board_02/footprint_geometry.json (CircuitOS:DHT22, four pads at 2.54 mm pitch); board_ir.json courtyard for U2 (8.2 x 15.6); Aosong AM2302 technical manual and Adafruit DHT22 datasheet (body 25.1 x 15.1 x 7.7 mm, 4 pins at 2.54 mm)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: There is no silkscreen on this board at all. The only F.SilkS string in board_02.kicad_pcb is the layer-table entry on line 20; there is no fp_line, fp_text, fp_rect or fp_arc on F.SilkS anywhere, and every footprint's Reference property is on F.Fab only. So nothing marks pin 1 on U1, U2, Q1, D1, R1, R2 or C1, nothing marks D1's cathode band, nothing outlines a single part body, and the assembler is given no reference designators to fit by. Because the footprints live in a library named CircuitOS that is not installed, KiCad also reports lib_footprint_issues for all eight, so not one footprint can be checked against a reference library either.
expected: Silkscreen outlines, pin-1 markers, the D1 cathode band and reference designators, plus a shippable footprint library.
evidence: evidence_board_02/facts_output.txt section 9; board_02.kicad_pcb (F.SilkS appears only at line 20; Reference properties all on F.Fab); evidence_board_02/drc_independent.json (8 lib_footprint_issues); evidence_board_02/render_top.png (kicad-cli 3D render of the top side: pads and copper only - no component bodies, no outlines, no designators, nothing to fit by)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board's own report contradicts itself. drc_summary.json says severity_error_violations: 0, and its by_type counts list only track_dangling (2), via_dangling (5) and lib_footprint_issues (8), with no entry for unconnected items at all - while drc.json in the same folder marks all five unconnected items severity error, four of them unconnected GND and one the RELAY_CTRL break. A reader of the summary alone would conclude the board is error-free. I reproduced the counts with my own kicad-cli run: 15 violations, all warning severity, plus 5 unconnected items, all error.
expected: A summary that counts the errors its own DRC file reports, including unconnected items.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: Every value in design_settings.rules of board_02.kicad_pro is 0.0 - min_clearance, min_track_width, min_via_diameter, min_through_hole_diameter, min_via_annular_width, min_copper_edge_clearance, min_hole_clearance, min_hole_to_hole - and rule_severities is empty. The board therefore carries no fab profile at all: its 0.8 mm holes in 1.3 mm pads (0.25 mm annular ring) and its 0.2 mm traces pass DRC because the checks that would reject them are switched off, not because they are acceptable. The 'check it before you would send it to a fab' step is present as a report but there is no profile in it to check against.
expected: A named fab profile's constraints - clearance, track width, annular ring, hole-to-hole, copper-to-edge - with severities set.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The GND zone's polygon is (0,0) (63.5,0) (63.5,45.72) (0,45.72) - exactly the Edge.Cuts gr_rect of the same board, which is (0,0) to (63.5,45.72). So even after a refill the pour runs right to the board outline with 0.0 mm copper-to-edge clearance, and because min_copper_edge_clearance is 0.0 the DRC cannot see it. A filled pour would be cut off by the router wherever it meets the edge.
expected: The pour pulled back from the board edge by the profile's copper-to-edge clearance.
evidence: evidence_board_02/facts_output.txt section 7; board_02.kicad_pcb line 611 (gr_rect) and line 1573 (zone polygon)

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The .kicad_pro gives net class power a 0.8 mm track width and applies it to GND, RELAY_COIL_NEG and VCC_5V, and class Default a 0.3 mm width for the rest, but the board contradicts its own classes: 16 of the 42 VCC_5V segments and 5 of the 14 RELAY_COIL_NEG segments are 0.2 mm wide, and 12 of 33 DHT22_DATA, 3 of 10 RELAY_CTRL and 3 of 12 TRANSISTOR_BASE segments are 0.2 mm as well. prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The 100 nF bypass C1 sits at (10.12,35.60), 12.1 mm from the ATmega's own supply pins (U1 pad 7 at (16.51,24.13), pad 8 at (16.51,21.59)); there is no capacitor at all across the relay coil or on the 5 V rail at the relay, where the coil current is switched; and the DHT22's 10 kOhm data pull-up R1 is 28 mm away on the far side of the board from the sensor it serves.
